title: ayam atma brahma — a week each
hook: ayam atma brahma — a week each
carry: ayam atma brahma — a week each
tomorrow: waking, dreaming, deep sleep. is there anything left after those?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ayam atma brahma in the Brihadaranyaka: this self is Brahman, made of all things, and as one acts, so one becomes. Today, back to the Mandukya, with one question.

A sleep app draws the night as a graph: light sleep, dreams, and a deep stretch near the bottom with nothing to report. Nobody wakes up and describes that part, because there seems to be nothing there to describe. So, one question: where are you, in the part of the night you never remember? The Mandukya stops right at that gap.
screen: `THE NIGHT AS A GRAPH.` → `NOTHING TO REPORT.` → `WHERE ARE YOU THEN?`

segments.voice: The Mandukya walks through the quarters of this self in order. Waking, which knows outward. Dreaming, which knows inward. Then the third. In paraphrase: where the sleeper wants no wanting and sees no dream, that is deep sleep. The one there has become one, a mass of knowing, made of bliss, enjoying bliss. Its name is prajna, the knowing one. Notice what the text refuses to say. It doesn't call deep sleep empty. It calls it gathered: everything folded into one, nothing wanted, nothing seen apart. Then it adds titles: the lord of all, the knower of all, the inner controller, the source where beings arise and come to rest. A neighbor tradition sings about the same stretch of night. A psalm in the Hebrew Bible, in the King James Version, says: "I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety." Here's what they share: sleep as a letting go, a peace nobody has to earn. And the honest difference. The psalmist lies down trusting the LORD, a thou who keeps the sleeper safe. The Mandukya says the gathered sleeper is this self, the one it has just called Brahman. Two old voices, each keeping watch over the quiet part of the night in its own words.
screen: `WAKING, DREAMING, DEEP SLEEP.` · `NOT EMPTY: GATHERED.` · `THE PSALM: LAY ME DOWN IN PEACE.` · then, large: `KEPT BY A THOU, OR FOUND AS THE SELF.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and let the body grow heavy, the way it does just before sleep, but stay awake. Let thoughts thin out without chasing them, and let wanting rest for a while. Notice the quiet that's left: not empty, just gathered.
Ayam atma brahma: this self, even in dreamless sleep, is a mass of knowing, and the Mandukya calls it the lord of all.
Keep this one: ayam atma brahma, a week each, and deep sleep isn't empty, it's gathered. Sleep well tonight.

howItsDone: In Vedanta study, the Mandukya's quarters of the self (waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and the fourth) are read with Gaudapada's verses. Psalm 4 is part of the Hebrew Bible, read by Jews and Christians.

original.note: Sanskrit: prajna, the knowing one, the Mandukya's name for this self in deep sleep.

what a scholar hears: Mandukya 5–6, prajnanaghana, anandamaya, prajna; read beside Psalm 4:8 without making them one teaching.

chat.meaning: Psalm 4:8 and the Mandukya both see deep rest as peace. The psalmist trusts the LORD who keeps him; the Mandukya says the gathered sleeper is this self.

Mandukya.meaning: a short Upanishad about Om and the quarters of the self

prajna.meaning: the knowing one: the self in deep sleep

psalm.meaning: a sacred song; here, Psalm 4 in the Hebrew Bible

sources.ref: Mandukya Upanishad 3–5 (waking, knowing outward; dreaming, knowing inward; deep sleep, where the sleeper desires no desire and sees no dream: become one, a mass of knowing, made of bliss, enjoying bliss, prajna)
Mandukya Upanishad 6 (this is the lord of all, the knower of all, the inner controller, the source of all, the arising and passing away of beings)

notes: Block 'ayam atma brahma — a week each', day 3 of 8 (1761–1768). Year 4 (day 1238, Gaudapada) taught waking, dream and deep sleep as a nightly cycle; this lesson stays with Mandukya 5–6 and the titles given to deep sleep.
Commentators differ on whether Mandukya 6 describes the prajna quarter itself or the Lord (Ishvara) seen through it; the lesson only reports the text's order. Confirm.

UNITY THREAD (wisdom day): Psalm 4:8 quoted from the KJV (4:9 in JPS numbering); please verify wording. Shared: sleep as a letting go, a peace nobody has to earn. Honest difference: the psalmist trusts the LORD who keeps the sleeper safe; the Mandukya says the gathered sleeper is this self, called Brahman. No ranking, no 'all the same'. A Jewish and a Christian reviewer should confirm the framing and the howItsDone line.
Priya storyline (1751–1764, day 13): the camp sleepover; a camper's mother has tucked a note with Psalm 4:8 into his bag (his family's tradition is left unnamed).
